findings.summary: The Bloom sizing constants (4.79 bits/item, k=3) are re-declared here, duplicating the identical private constants already in BloomConstructionTest (M2.5) with no shared source of truth.
findings.failure_scenario: A future revision of the FPR target updates one file's constant and misses the other -- FilterCandidates keeps sizing Bloom filters to the old target while the property test keeps passing against the new one, silently drifting apart.

findings.summary: The canonical constructor only catches IOException from MembershipFilter.decode() to produce a friendly IllegalArgumentException; RunLength.decode can throw an unchecked IndexOutOfBoundsException on a pathological uvarint run causing int overflow in BitSet.set(from, to), which would propagate uncaught.
findings.failure_scenario: new SegmentKey(..., "R" + base64url(bytes encoding two uvarint runs near Integer.MAX_VALUE)) overflows pos+run to negative inside RunLength.decode, throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the intended IllegalArgumentException. Unreachable via any call site this diff adds (SegmentPublisher always passes a freshly-encoded, trusted filter string), but becomes reachable once M2.7 constructs SegmentKey from a previously-persisted, untrusted key string.

findings.summary: The backlog's 'verified against a real OpenSearch node' claim is substantiated by OffsetMonotonicityIT/RestartResumeIT/DeleteAndVersionIT (which do use the real DefaultIngest->SegmentPublisher path), not by SearchableIT, which builds its SegmentKey via the legacy 5-arg constructor and never exercises chooseFilter/FilterCandidates/registeredCount.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in SegmentPublisher.chooseFilter that only manifests against a running node would not be caught by SearchableIT, since that test never constructs a key through the changed code path.
